title: App Service Scaling and Autoscale
description: Configure scale up, scale out, and autoscale rules so your App Service app handles traffic changes automatically.

data.text: Scaling ensures your app stays responsive as traffic changes. In App Service, you can scale up (get a bigger VM), scale out (add more VMs), or use autoscale rules that adjust capacity automatically based on metrics or a schedule.

rows: Increases CPU and memory per instance
Your app needs more power on a single server
Adds more instances behind a load balancer
Your app needs to handle more concurrent requests
Automatically scales out or in based on rules
Traffic changes throughout the day or week

data.text: You scale up by changing the App Service plan SKU. You scale out by increasing the instance count in the plan. Autoscale combines both ideas: it can increase instance count, and you can pair it with a plan SKU upgrade when needed.
Autoscale rules use metrics such as CPU percentage, memory, disk queue length, or HTTP queue length. You set minimum and maximum instance counts so Azure never scales too far up or down.

data.title: Autoscale JSON Rule
data.content: Autoscale profile that adds instances when CPU exceeds 70 percent

data.text: You can create separate autoscale profiles for different times. For example, use more instances during business hours and fewer at night. This is called schedule-based scaling.

data.title: Common Schedule Patterns
items: Increase instances Monday through Friday, 8 AM to 8 PM
Prepare for expected spikes such as marketing campaigns or product launches

data.caption: How autoscale evaluates traffic and adjusts instances
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[App Service App] --> B[Metrics Collector]
    B --> C{CPU > 70% for 5 min?}
    C -->|Yes| D[Add Instance]
    C -->|No| E{CPU < 30% for 5 min?}
    E -->|Yes| F[Remove Instance]
    E -->|No| G[Keep Current Count]
    D --> H[Cooldown: 5 Minutes]
    F --> H
    H --> B

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Scale up for more power per instance; scale out for more requests.
Autoscale uses metrics such as CPU percentage and HTTP queue length.
Set minimum and maximum instances to control cost and availability.
Schedule-based scaling lets you plan capacity for known traffic patterns.
data.takeaway: Autoscale keeps your app responsive while avoiding over-provisioning and unnecessary cost.
